summary: Near the run's time boundary, with all obligations disposed and no pending work, this small sourced step traces how a follower legally reaches the state the installSnapshot finding depends on, which also answers the compacted-leader variant left open for the truncation-failure finding. Submission is a feedback-only research product (no map version). Argument: sendLatestSnapshot is entered exactly when setupAppendEntries returns ErrLogNotFound (replication.go 222-232), which happens when the leader's own log no longer holds an index at or below nextIndex, i.e. the leader compacted past the point where it and the follower diverge; in that case the leader does not keep walking nextIndex down to 1 but ships its latest snapshot at index S. A follower can carry a watermark above S when its log has a divergent tail longer than the leader's snapshot - a partitioned former leader with uncommitted entries, or a follower left stale-high by the confirmed truncation-failure gap - so the two confirmed findings compose: the store-failure gap can supply the stale-high watermark and the leader's compaction supplies the InstallSnapshot at an index below it, landing directly in the installSnapshot watermark case measured by check 58ebdb2f92184614b01ecfab56fe2bc9. Consequently the earlier 'stuck at nextIndex 1' outcome applies only while the leader still holds the index the follower lacks; once the leader's log is compacted, the route leads into the snapshot path and then into the installSnapshot case. The feedback states plainly that this is a reading argument, that no execution witness rolls the two mechanisms together in one process, that compaction timing relative to a divergent tail was not measured, that the non-monotonic compaction variant was reasoned but not exercised, and that nothing in the transport or replication reading was evaluated for defects; the run's recorded results remain three confirmed in-scope violations plus one reviewed bounded no-violation. Preflight validation returns valid with no diagnostics.
